newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: D'Amato not attending Swiss Holocaust conference.
newsitem.headline: D'Amato not attending Swiss Holocaust conference.

text.p: U.S. Senator Alfonse D'Amato, who has fronted the inquiries into the unclaimed riches of Holocaust victims, will not attend this week's Geneva conference on looted Nazi gold, art and property, organisers said on Monday.

The U.S.-based Jewish human rights group Simon Wiesenthal Centre had initially announced that D'Amato, who accuses Swiss banks of hoarding the wealth of Jews murdered by Hitler, would attend the June 24-25 international conference.
But the centre's dean, Martin Hier, told a news conference that the New York republican, who chairs the U.S. Senate Banking Committee, had to stay home during tax bill discussions at the house.
Political, academic, legal and clerical personalities from Europe, Israel, the United States and Latin America are expected to attend the Geneva conference.

The Wiesenthal centre is also expanding its hunt to other countries that were neutral during World War Two as well as to Latin America and the central bank vaults of the former Allies, which hold some 5.5 tonnes of gold stolen and recovered.
D'Amato is the scourge of many Swiss who feel that he is unfairly characterising their Alpine country's neutrality during World War Two as complicity.
Switzerland's neutrality in the middle of warring Europe has come under fierce international criticism as little more than collaboration with the Nazis under a different name.
But the drumbeat criticism from abroad has radicalised opposition to government efforts of compensation by appealing to Swiss national pride and sovereignty.
A scathing U.S. government report compiled by U.S. Under-secretary of Commerce Stuart Eizenstat and published in May, which alleged the Swiss were bankers to the Nazis, has also outraged many Swiss.
